name: Train on SageMaker (managed compute)
desc: Submit a non-blocking managed training job from a DataFrame, poll it, load the model, then score — scale out when training needs a bigger machine or GPU

## 🛰️ Train on SageMaker (managed compute)

`train_model` runs **inside the VM**, bounded by its memory, CPU, and the cell timeout. When you need a **bigger/GPU machine** or training would blow the cell clock, hand the work to **SageMaker-managed compute** instead — same feature/target contract, bigger machine. This recipe trains from an **in-VM DataFrame** (`sm_train` uploads it to S3 for you). If the training set is itself **too big to pull into the VM**, use the *Train on SageMaker from S3* recipe instead — it UNLOADs the data to S3 and trains straight off a pointer, so the rows never enter the sandbox.

The key difference from `train_model`: **`sm_train` is non-blocking**. It uploads your data + a preprocessing recipe to S3, kicks off a managed Training Job, and returns a **handle in seconds** while training runs off-box. So the submit, the poll, and the load each live in their **own cell** you run in sequence — do NOT expect results in the submit cell.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Labelled DataFrame"] --> T["sm_train (returns in seconds)"]
  T -. runs on managed compute .-> J["SageMaker Training Job"]
  J -->|sm_training_job_status| C{"Completed?"}
  C -->|no · wait ~30s · re-run| C
  C -->|yes| L["sm_load_model → model in VM"]
  L --> P["predict_batch → scored catalog"]
```

**When to reach for this:** small/fast tabular that fits the VM → `train_model` (instant, in-VM, the default). Fits the VM but needs a GPU / long training → `sm_train(df, …)` (this recipe). Training set too big to pull into the VM → the *Train on SageMaker from S3* recipe.

**Cost & timing:** a job takes minutes (instance spin-up alone is ~3–4 min) and you pay for the minutes it runs. Nothing bills after it finishes — there is **no standing endpoint** in this recipe (see the *Deploy a real-time endpoint* recipe for that). If SageMaker isn't configured in this environment, the `sm_*` helpers raise a clear error and you can fall back to `train_model`.

# 1) Load your labelled data (Athena / S3 / DynamoDB). This is the SAME feature +
#    target contract as train_model (target=, features=, categorical=, numeric=),
#    so you can prototype in-VM with train_model and scale out with sm_train later.
df = read_athena("SELECT * FROM <your_table> LIMIT 50000")
print(df.shape, "rows × cols")
df.head()

# 2) SUBMIT the job — NON-BLOCKING. Returns a handle in ~seconds while training runs
#    on its own instance. Do NOT put the load/score in THIS cell — it isn't ready yet.
#    Trains a scikit-learn Pipeline (estimator='random_forest' by default — see the
#    next cell for the estimator menu). Optional: instance= (e.g. 'ml.m5.2xlarge'),
#    n_estimators=, max_depth=, task=, features=.
job = sm_train(df, target="<target_column>")
print("submitted:", job)

# 2b) PICK THE ESTIMATOR — sm_train trains a complete Pipeline(preprocess ->
#     estimator) on SageMaker and brings it back as a stock .joblib (plain
#     joblib.load, RAW-row contract). Choose from the menu via estimator=:
#       random_forest (default) · gradient_boosting · xgboost · lightgbm
#       · logistic · linear · ridge      (logistic/linear/ridge are task-aware)
#     The gradient-boosting trio (gradient_boosting/xgboost/lightgbm) are the strong
#     tabular defaults. Optional: scale=True to StandardScaler the numerics;
#     n_estimators=, max_depth=, C=, alpha= tune them.
#   job = sm_train(df, target="<target_column>", estimator="xgboost")   # or lightgbm/...
#   print("submitted:", job)

# 3) POLL until it finishes — RE-RUN this cell every ~30s. Status walks
#    'InProgress (Nm elapsed)' → 'Completed (Nm)' (or 'Failed: <reason>').
#    Only move on to step 4 once it reads Completed.
print(sm_training_job_status(job))

# 4) Load the finished model back into the VM. sm_load_model WAITS for the job,
#    then returns a complete scikit-learn Pipeline that takes RAW rows exactly like
#    a train_model Pipeline (plain joblib.load — no rewrap). If the estimator is
#    xgboost/lightgbm, its library is auto-installed in the VM on load. Inspect it:
model = sm_load_model(job)
model_info(model)

# 5) Score with it. predict / predict_batch accept EITHER a loaded model OR the job
#    handle directly (a job is auto-resolved via sm_load_model), so it's the SAME
#    prediction surface for local and SageMaker-trained models.
scored = predict_batch(job, df, output_col="prediction")
scored.head()
